How far "$500,000 Cashword" is through its run does not decide anything by itself. It changes how closely to look at the other numbers.

Today's free summary of "$500,000 Cashword" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
1118.headline: Close to two months, no top prize claimed

1124.body:
"Spectacular Riches" has had no $2 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "Spectacular Riches" comes from official Ohio lottery numbers, current through November 25.
1124.headline: Good news: no big claims

1125.body:
"$1,000,000 Black Titanium" has three of five top prizes left and is near the midpoint of its run. About a third of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Everything above about "$1,000,000 Black Titanium" comes from the Ohio Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
1125.headline: Tickets sold so far

1127.body:
"Triple Tripler" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $1,800 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold nineteen of the original twenty. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

The numbers for "Triple Tripler" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
1127.headline: The top prize list got shorter

1134.body:
"Crazy Cash" has 625,247 prizes of $1 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $100 prize, with 1,401 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Every line of Crazy Cash's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
1134.headline: A close look at the prizes

1140.body:
"$25, $50 or $250" has 592,067 prizes of $25 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $50 prize, with 118,367 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If "$25, $50 or $250" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
1140.headline: A close look at the prizes

696.body:
The top prize count on "Monopoly 200X" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of ten top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

If you play "Monopoly 200X" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
696.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

762.body:
"Billion" is well into its run, with about a third of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Each day without a top prize claim on "Billion", the remaining top prizes are spread across fewer unsold tickets. The number of tickets printed is fixed.

The numbers for "Billion" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
762.headline: Where this game is in its run

827.body:
Most of the tickets for "50th Anniversary" are sold. The top prize count has held, with one of three still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "50th Anniversary" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
827.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

847.body:
Before you buy "Bingo 50X", know that its $500,000 top prize is gone. The game still pays many smaller prizes, but the biggest one left is $100,000. That is still a sizable prize, but much smaller than the one shown on the ticket.

Every line of Bingo 50X's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
847.headline: The advertised top prize is gone

891.body:
"Cash Explosion 25X" has 82,880 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with one left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything above about "Cash Explosion 25X" comes from the Ohio Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
891.headline: What the prize table shows
